title: Bounded efficacy errors permit safe release allocation in two selected mouse contact models
abstract: We tested a release allocation rule with bounded errors between contact size and mean efficacy. We used 1,519 Allen V1DD connections and 1,472 MICrONS connections. Independent Bernoulli events, exact local mean compensation and a fixed expected event count were assumed. We minimized the largest variance difference from uniform release over independent efficacy intervals. At mean probability 0.5 and error factor 1.25, strict gains held in 86.90 and 92.05 percent of connections, against 57.01 and 69.70 percent for the earlier nominal rule. Mean guaranteed margins were 14.50 and 19.14 percent of nominal uniform variance. These are not worst-case relative percentage reductions. We prove that a strict benefit is possible exactly when the largest-to-smallest size ratio exceeds the squared error factor. All allocations passed convex optimality checks; independent synthetic constrained fits and exhaustive corners agreed. The result is a model benchmark, not evidence for biological release allocation. Exact compensation, independent release, uncertain weights, one animal per map and no activity data limit biological use. Code, aggregate results, provenance and a figure support reproduction. External contact records are not bundled.

display.caption: Guaranteed variance margins and strict-benefit fractions at mean event probability 0.5. Margins use nominal uniform variance as their unit. Lines describe selected contacts under model assumptions, not animal confidence limits.
